parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
What is the overall trend in UK real expenditure on alcohol purchased in shops for
consumption off the premises between 2008 quarter 1 and 2012 quarter 2?

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Explain how a change in one demand factor might have caused the change in weekly
alcohol consumption for the ‘average for all age groups’ shown in Table 1.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Identify the age group that has shown the greatest change in average weekly alcohol
consumption between 2006 and 2010.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
For the age group you have identified, explain one possible economic reason for the
change in its average weekly alcohol consumption compared with the other age groups.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
If the minimum price per unit were fixed at 50 pence rather than 45 pence, explain, with the
help of a diagram, how the higher price would affect the consumer surplus in this market.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Explain, with reference to the data, how crime and hospital admissions arising from excessive
alcohol consumption contribute to social costs.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Discuss whether the problems associated with excessive alcohol consumption are better
dealt with through a minimum price per unit for alcohol rather than through an education
campaign. 
Section B
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Show how the economic problem can be explained with the use of a production possibility
curve.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Discuss whether an outward shift in a country’s production possibility curve will always raise
the welfare of the citizens of that country.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Explain why an increase in the money supply and rising world energy prices are categorised
as different causes of inflation in an economy.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Discuss whether a floating exchange rate is consistent with the policy objective of a low and
stable rate of inflation.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Explain how comparative advantage shows that specialisation and international trade can
improve the welfare of consumers in an economy.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Discuss whether an economy would benefit more from an unfavourable rather than a
favourable movement in its terms of trade.
